behavior_description: After junit-platform-surefire-provider changed from 1.0.3 to 1.3.2, the paris module failed before executing its tests. The updated provider 1.3.2 brings Surefire runtime components surefire-api 2.22.0 and common-java5 2.22.0, while the project still uses maven-surefire-plugin 2.19.1. During test execution Maven reported java.lang.NoSuchMethodError for org.apache.maven.surefire.util.internal.StringUtils.requireNonNull(Object). This is a runtime binary/linkage incompatibility in the testing infrastructure rather than a behavioral change in the client program.
notes: PRE completed 32 tests with 0 failures and 0 errors and BUILD SUCCESS. BREAKING completed 26 tests successfully in earlier modules, then the paris module started 0 tests and Maven ended with BUILD FAILURE. PRE paris configuration used maven-surefire-plugin 2.19.1 with junit-platform-surefire-provider 1.0.3. Provider 1.0.3 depends on surefire-api 2.19.1 and common-java5 2.19.1. BREAKING kept maven-surefire-plugin 2.19.1 but changed the provider to 1.3.2, which depends on surefire-api 2.22.0 and common-java5 2.22.0. The breaking plugin realm therefore contains mixed Surefire versions. common-java5 2.22.0 contains org.apache.maven.surefire.util.internal.StringUtils but its version does not contain requireNonNull(Object). Maven reports NoSuchMethodError for that method. Classified as runtime binary/linkage incompatibility and NON_BEHAVIORAL.

behavior_description: After slf4j-api changed from 1.7.36 to 2.0.2, SLF4J ignored the old 1.7-style StaticLoggerBinder provided by slf4j-mock 2.2.0 and returned org.slf4j.helpers.NOPLogger. The unchanged slf4j-mock 2.2.0 testing library expected a ProxyMock logger and explicitly cast the logger instance to org.simplify4u.slf4jmock.ProxyMock. The cast therefore failed with java.lang.ClassCastException. The project compiled successfully, but 12 tests ended with runtime errors because of the changed runtime logging behavior.
notes: PRE used slf4j-api 1.7.36 and slf4j-mock 2.2.0 and completed 38 tests with 0 failures and 0 errors, BUILD SUCCESS. BREAKING changed only slf4j-api to 2.0.2 while slf4j-mock remained 2.2.0. BREAKING completed 38 tests with 0 failures and 12 errors, BUILD FAILURE. SLF4J reported that the StaticLoggerBinder from slf4j-mock targets SLF4J 1.7.x and was ignored. slf4j-mock LoggerAnnotationEngine.findLoggersMocks reads the logger field and performs a cast to ProxyMock. With SLF4J 2.0.2 the runtime logger was NOPLogger, causing ClassCastException. No binary linkage error such as NoSuchMethodError or NoClassDefFoundError was observed. Classified provisionally as behavioral pending independent second review.

behavior_description: After poi-ooxml changed from 4.1.2 to 5.1.0, the project still kept org.apache.poi:poi and poi-scratchpad at 4.1.2. The new poi-ooxml 5.1.0 expects POI 5.1.0-compatible runtime types. In the breaking runtime, POIXMLTextExtractor from poi-ooxml 5.1.0 is an interface extending POITextExtractor, while POITextExtractor from poi 4.1.2 is an abstract class. This class/interface mismatch causes document extraction to fail at runtime. The affected tests then receive null extracted text and fail assertions. This is a binary/runtime dependency incompatibility rather than a semantic behavioral change in the client program.
notes: PRE uses poi 4.1.2, poi-scratchpad 4.1.2, and poi-ooxml 4.1.2 and ends in BUILD SUCCESS. BREAKING changes only poi-ooxml to 5.1.0 while poi and poi-scratchpad remain 4.1.2. The breaking log shows 'POIXMLTextExtractor can not implement POITextExtractor, because it is not an interface' and also a ClassNotFoundException for org.apache.poi.poifs.crypt.agile.AgileEncryptionInfoBuilder. javap confirmed POITextExtractor in poi 4.1.2 is an abstract class, while POIXMLTextExtractor in poi-ooxml 5.1.0 is an interface extending it. The poi-ooxml 5.1.0 POM explicitly depends on poi 5.1.0. Classified as NON_BEHAVIORAL binary/runtime linkage incompatibility.

behavior_description: Updating org.graalvm.js:js-scriptengine from 22.3.2 to 23.0.1 changes GraalJSEngineFactory from Java 11-compatible bytecode (class file major version 55) to Java 17 bytecode (class file major version 61). The project still runs on Java 11, which supports class file versions only up to 55. When the updated class is loaded during test setup, the JVM throws UnsupportedClassVersionError. This is a runtime platform/class-version compatibility failure rather than a semantic behavioral change.
notes: PRE: js-scriptengine 22.3.2; javap shows GraalJSEngineFactory major version 55, compatible with Java 11. PRE runs 80 tests with 0 failures, 0 errors, 1 skipped and BUILD SUCCESS. BREAKING: js-scriptengine 23.0.1; javap shows GraalJSEngineFactory major version 61, which corresponds to Java 17 bytecode. The breaking Docker image runs OpenJDK 11.0.19, which supports class file versions only up to 55. The breaking log reports java.lang.UnsupportedClassVersionError for GraalJSEngineFactory and finishes with 80 tests, 0 failures, 79 errors, 1 skipped, BUILD FAILURE. Classified as NON_BEHAVIORAL runtime/platform compatibility failure.

behavior_description: Updating jackson-databind from 2.10.5.1 to 2.14.1 creates an incompatible Jackson dependency combination. The project continues to resolve jackson-core and jackson-annotations 2.10.5 while jackson-databind becomes 2.14.1. jackson-databind 2.14.1 requires com.fasterxml.jackson.core.util.JacksonFeature, but that class is not present in jackson-core 2.10.5. Test execution therefore stops with NoClassDefFoundError before meaningful application behavior can be compared.
notes: PRE: 16 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, BUILD SUCCESS. PRE dependency tree resolves jackson-core 2.10.5, jackson-annotations 2.10.5, and jackson-databind 2.10.5.1. BREAKING: 16 tests, 0 failures, 16 errors, BUILD FAILURE. BREAKING dependency tree resolves jackson-core 2.10.5, jackson-annotations 2.10.5, and jackson-databind 2.14.1. The first meaningful error is java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError for com/fasterxml/jackson/core/util/JacksonFeature, originating from jackson-databind DatatypeFeatures.defaultFeatures. Direct JAR inspection confirms JacksonFeature.class is absent from jackson-core 2.10.5 and present in jackson-core 2.14.1. Evaluation of the jackson-databind 2.14.1 POM confirms jackson.version.core=2.14.1. Classified as NON_BEHAVIORAL binary/runtime dependency incompatibility.

behavior_description: Updating Mockito from 4.11.0 to 5.1.1 changes the default MockMaker from the subclass-based ByteBuddyMockMaker to InlineByteBuddyMockMaker. The affected test uses mocked Generator instances where Generator.shrink is a final method. Under Mockito 4.11.0, the final shrink method is not intercepted by the default subclass mock maker, so the real shrink method executes and reaches the stubbed doShrink method, returning [3, 6]. Under Mockito 5.1.1, the default inline mock maker intercepts the final shrink method. Because shrink itself is not stubbed, the mock returns an empty list, changing the observed test result from [3, 6] to [].
notes: PRE with mockito-core 4.11.0: 510 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 18 skipped, BUILD SUCCESS. BREAKING with mockito-core 5.1.1: 510 tests, 1 failure, 0 errors, 18 skipped, BUILD FAILURE. Failing test: CompositeGeneratorTest.shrinkingChoosesAComponentCapableOfShrinkingTheValue. Assertion expected [3, 6] but actual result was []. Generator.shrink(SourceOfRandomness,Object) is final and calls doShrink. Mockito 4.11.0 DefaultMockitoPlugins maps MockMaker to org.mockito.internal.creation.bytebuddy.ByteBuddyMockMaker, while Mockito 5.1.1 maps MockMaker to org.mockito.internal.creation.bytebuddy.InlineByteBuddyMockMaker. No project-specific mockito-extensions override exists. Causal validation: using Mockito 5.1.1 but forcing mock-maker-subclass makes the exact failing test pass with 1 test, 0 failures, 0 errors, BUILD SUCCESS. Classified as PROVISIONAL_BEHAVIORAL pending independent review.

PRE build succeeds. In the PRE messaging module, jackson-databind 2.9.10.8 and jackson-core 2.9.10 coexist with jackson-annotations 2.11.2 without failure. After updating jackson-databind to 2.13.1, the messaging module resolves jackson-databind 2.13.1 and jackson-core 2.13.1 while jackson-annotations remains at 2.11.2. The breaking build executes 12 tests with 1 failure and 5 errors. All affected tests are caused by java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError for com/fasterxml/jackson/annotation/JsonKey. Direct JAR inspection confirmed JsonKey.class is absent from jackson-annotations 2.11.2 and present in jackson-annotations 2.13.1. The apparent assertion failure also wraps the same NoClassDefFoundError. Therefore this is classified as NON_BEHAVIORAL because the failure is caused by a mixed-version Jackson runtime/binary dependency incompatibility, not an observable semantic behavior change.

behavior_description: After updating slf4j-api from 1.7.36 to 2.0.1, SLF4J no longer uses the existing Logback 1.7-style binding. The old binding is ignored and SLF4J falls back to the NOP logger implementation. Client test code expects a ch.qos.logback.classic.Logger and casts the returned logger, causing java.lang.ClassCastException.
notes: PRE build using slf4j-api 1.7.36 completes successfully. EventMessageHandlerTest runs 8 tests with 0 failures and 0 errors. The complete PRE build runs 726 tests successfully. After updating to slf4j-api 2.0.1, SLF4J reports that no SLF4J providers were found and that the existing logback-classic 1.2.11 binding targeting SLF4J 1.7.x is ignored. SLF4J therefore defaults to the NOP logger. EventMessageHandlerTest.setUp then attempts to cast org.slf4j.helpers.NOPLogger to ch.qos.logback.classic.Logger, causing java.lang.ClassCastException. Additional Dropwizard tests fail during class initialization because the logger context cannot be acquired. The later NoClassDefFoundError 'Could not initialize class' messages are secondary effects of failed class initialization and are not evidence of a missing class. BREAKING runs 726 tests with 0 failures and 12 errors. No binary linkage incompatibility was identified. Reviewer 1 therefore classifies this case as PROVISIONAL_BEHAVIORAL pending independent second review.

behavior_description: After updating Apache Commons IO from 2.7 to 2.11.0, FileUtils.copyFile() throws IllegalArgumentException when the source path refers to a directory rather than a regular file. The client method copyCustomResources() catches IOException and converts it into ValidationException, but does not catch IllegalArgumentException. As a result, the new exception escapes and causes a previously passing test to fail.
notes: PRE: commons-io 2.7, BUILD SUCCESS, 345 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 2 skipped. ReportBuilderTest runs 25 tests successfully. BREAKING: commons-io 2.11.0, BUILD FAILURE, 345 tests, 0 failures, 1 error. The affected test is copyCustomResources_OnDirAsFile_ThrowsIOException. The test passes a directory 'src/test/resources/js' to copyCustomResources() and expects ValidationException. In the breaking version, FileUtils.copyFile() throws java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Parameter 'srcFile' is not a file. The exception originates at org.apache.commons.io.FileUtils.requireFile() and propagates through FileUtils.copyFile() to ReportBuilder.copyCustomResources(ReportBuilder.java:174). The client catches FileNotFoundException and IOException, but not IllegalArgumentException. This is evidence of an exception-behavior change, rather than binary linkage incompatibility. Reviewer 1 classification is PROVISIONAL_BEHAVIORAL. Final classification requires independent second review. A repair has not yet been implemented or verified.
